item.title: Weekly Newsletter #9 — January 20, 2026
item.description:
📣 COMMENT AT SEPTA BOARD MEETING

There's a SEPTA board meeting coming up this Thursday at 3pm. We'll be there--will you join us?

We'll be speaking about the status of the New Bus Network, real-time arrival signs, and a dedicated trolley diversion route.

SEPTA board meetings are key chances for riders to push SEPTA leadership for promised system improvements and policies that expand transit access and improve reliability. Public testimony helps to hold SEPTA leadership accountable, and even brief comments can make a difference to how the system functions.

SIGN UP HERE

🚲 BIKE USAGE IS UP

The Bicycle Coalition’s bike count data is out and the numbers look great!

Bike trips in 2025 increased 10% from last year. And if you include e-scooters, total micromobility trips increased 12.2%.

👋 THANKS FOR COMING TO OUR MEETUP

We had a great time this past Thursday at our Urbanist PowerPoint Party Meetup. More than 100 of you showed up to hear presentations from experts on a range of interesting topics. Thanks for coming!

🚌 SEPTA IS GETTING SAFER

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

EVENTS

January Day of Action: Transit Leadership Training
January 22, 5:30pm - 7:30pm | Transit Forward Philly/BCGP Office, 1500 Walnut St, Ste 1107
Join Transit Forward Philadelphia for a transit leadership training. You'll learn how you can rally your community to make transit more affordable, safer, accessible, and fully funded.

Tiny WPA 10th Anniversary Celebration
Feb 12 from 6pm to 9pm | 3145 West Jefferson Street
Join Tiny WPA for a benefit celebrating their 10th anniversary featuring music, an open bar, delicious bites, and a live auction. Come support their work make Philadelphia's public spaces better.

Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Conference
Fri, Feb 20, at 8:30 AM | The Study at University City, 20 S 33rd St
The Future of Cities Conference is a student-led, faculty-advised conference that aims to bring together urban innovators and experts from the public and private sectors to challenge and deepen the discourse around the trends, technologies, and policies transforming the future of our cities

WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

  • Inquirer.com / Zillow says the Philly region will be one of the 10 hottest housing markets of 2026
  • The Hill / Don’t let this housing crisis go to waste

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

  • Inquirer.com / The Avenue of the Arts to break ground on an ambitious $150 million streetscape to make Broad Street greener
  • Inquirer.com / Keeping seniors fit in Philly takes a citywide effort | Expert Opinion

🚌 TRANSIT

  • Billy Penn at WHYY / Crime on SEPTA fell again last year — to historic lows
  • WHYY / ‘Going to make my life much better’: SEPTA trolley riders react to tunnel reopening
  • worksinprogress.co / The United States needs fewer bus stops
  • usa.streetsblog.org / Passenger Rail Is Headed for a Reckoning — and the First 90 Days of 2026 Will Decide It

🚲 MOBILITY

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #8 — January 14, 2026
item.description:
🤝 MEETUP TOMORROW

Join us TOMORROW, Thursday, 1/15 at 6pm for our next meetup, an urbanist PowerPoint party!

RSVP NOW

🚏 INTERCITY BUS TERMINAL RETURNING IN MAY

Mayor Parker has officially signed into law a funding plan for the revitalization of Philadelphia's former Greyhound intercity bus terminal -- and we were there!

🚋 TROLLEY TUNNEL REOPENING

After a 2-month closure and impacts to 60,000 riders -- The trolley tunnel is finally open again!

We held a fun and impromptu Welcome Home party with our partners at Transit Forward Philly during Monday's morning rush!

Thank you also to everyone who helped advocate for  speeding up the surface diversion routing for trolley riders. SEPTA and the City have heard our demands and followed through with a few changes to speed up service. We are following up to make sure transit priority measures stay in place for future diversions.

🏘️ HOUSING FOR HAHNEMANN

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

Fortunately, a developer has secured permits for 361 units on the site with ground-floor commercial, but CM Young's overlay would also ban housing in the surrounding parcels--tell him we want housing for Hahnemann!

SAY NO TO HOMES BAN

🏢 POINT ACCESS BLOCKS

Point access blocks are a great way to increase the supply of housing that's both more affordable and more liveable. These single-stair buildings allow for human-scale urban infill with better floorplans and even improved fire safety.

If you're unfamiliar, AIA Philadelphia put together an interesting guide to the housing typology here.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer: Hahnemann developer secures permits for apartments in advance of Council housing ban

But the tradition of “councilmanic prerogative” would likely guarantee its passage because other Council members are unlikely to vote against a bill that affects only one district.

Nevertheless, the housing and transit advocacy group 5th Square has begun a campaign against the legislation and issued a petition earlier this week calling for its withdrawal.

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #7 — January 6, 2026
item.description:
🚫🏘️ NO HAHNEMANN HOME BAN

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital. (Bill # 251101)

Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

YES TO MORE HOMES

 

The site at Broad and Race Streets lies on top of an express subway stop, and benefits from proximity to Center City jobs, shops, and cultural amenities. Since the shuttering of Hahnemann in 2019, the site currently provides little value to Philadelphians or tax dollars to the City, despite its central location.

We support mixed-use development for this site to protect neighbors from rising housing costs, grow transit ridership, and support local workers and businesses.

🤝 MEETUP NEXT WEEK

Join us next week on Thursday, 1/15 for our next meetup, an urbanist PowerPoint party!

RSVP NOW

☁️ CLEAN AIR FOR GRAYS FERRY

The Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) is currently constructing a 7-story parking garage in Grays Ferry with over 1,000 parking spaces.

CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS). However, CHOP has not yet received the permit and AMS has not opened an official public comment period.

You can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about this proposal that would bring additional air pollution to South Philadelphia’s Grays Ferry neighborhood.

TAKE ACTION

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🦺 BECOME A VISION ZERO AMBASSADOR

The City of Philadelphia's Vision Zero program is looking for ambassadors for its 2026 cohort.

VZ ambassadors help spread the word about Vision Zero and traffic safety amongst friends, neighbors, and groups they are part of and act as the voice of their community around traffic safety issues.

Applications are open until Sunday, February 1, and those who complete the program will receive a $1750 stipend.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏙️ Philly2050 Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is looking to hear from you about what you want for the future of the city. We encourage you to respond in support of key urbanist issues like transit-oriented housing, walkable neighborhoods, expansion of transit options, protected bike lanes, and more.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

🚫🏘️ NO HAHNEMANN HOME BAN

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital. (Bill # 251101)

Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

YES TO MORE HOMES

 

The site at Broad and Race Streets lies on top of an express subway stop, and benefits from proximity to Center City jobs, shops, and cultural amenities. Since the shuttering of Hahnemann in 2019, the site currently provides little value to Philadelphians or tax dollars to the City, despite its central location.

We support mixed-use development for this site to protect neighbors from rising housing costs, grow transit ridership, and support local workers and businesses.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #5 — December 9, 2025
item.description:
🎉 FRIDAY: HOLIDAY PARTY

This Friday, December 12th, join us for our holiday party and awards ceremony!

Celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

We will also be presenting awards to the winners of the 2025 Urbanist Awards!

🚋 SPEED UP DIVERTED TROLLEYS

Since mid-November 2025, West Philly Trolleys are diverting to 40th and Market due to overhead wire problems in the tunnel.

These trolleys are frequently stuck in University City traffic, especially on Spruce, 38th, and 40th Streets – delaying over 30,000 daily riders.

There are up to 10 times more trolley riders than cars using these streets!

SIGN HERE to tell the City & SEPTA to prioritize riders during EVERY extended trolley diversion and;

  • Create temporary transitways on Spruce, 38th, and 40th Streets
  • Divert vehicle traffic during rush hours & restrict parking
  • Give traffic-signal priority to SEPTA vehicles
  • Provide shelter and benches for waiting riders, especially at 40th & Market
  • Improve bus frequencies in affected areas

🍽️ SUPPORT OUTDOOR DINING

We love our city's streeteries, but unfortunately extensive red tape makes it difficult and expensive for a restaurant to offer outdoor dining.

You can help change that by coming to City Hall on Thursday, December 11th to speak in support of expanding outdoor dining in Philly.

🏘️ HOME PLAN

We are excited to see the HOME plan put a focus on housing investment and policy change and we have some thoughts to share about how the plan can be made even better.

See here for our full statement, but the highlights are:

  • Create a fast-track for affordable housing permits
  • Loosen restrictions around SROs, ADUs, and smaller infill projects 
  • Encourage transit-oriented communities through zoning reform
  • Create a stronger right for tenants to pursue fair rents and housing improvements
  • Provide housing opportunities in all neighborhoods of the city

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏙️ Philly2050 Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is looking to hear from you about what you want for the future of the city. We encourage you to respond in support of key urbanist issues like transit-oriented housing, walkable neighborhoods, expansion of transit options, protected bike lanes, and more.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

🚲 Parking-Protected Bike Lane Petition

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal in PA! The Bicycle Coalition is fighting for their legalization. Sign their petition to show your support for safer bike lanes!

EVENTS

Book Club: When Driving Is Not an Option
Wednesday December 3rd • 5:30 pm | Bicycle Coalition 8th Floor Amenity Room, 1500 Walnut St
Join us, the Bicycle Coalition, and Philly Bike Action for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action) with pizza served for dinner.

SEPTA Holiday Bus Display
December 06, at 11:00am - 12pm | Love Park, 1501 JFK Blvd
SEPTA is hosting it’s annual Holiday Bus Display and People’s Choice Awards at Love Park. Join Transit Forward Philly as they check out the decorated buses and share ways that people can take action to support transit.

5th Square Holiday Party + Annual Urbanist Awards Ceremony
Friday, December 12th at 7 PM | Indy Hall, 709 N 2nd St
Join 5th Square members and friends for our Holiday Party + Urbanist Awards Ceremony where we will be presenting awards to members of our community for their outstanding contributions to Philadelphia’s urbanist movement.

Transit Forward Philly: December Day of Action
December 15, at 5:30pm - 7pm | 1500 Walnut, Suite 1107
Join Transit Forward Philly as they make care packages for transit workers and riders in Philly to share our gratitude for all that they do to help Philadelphians move around the region and make up our transit community.
